_doc: Casting Salt Creek's voices (docs/briefs/voice-casting.md). Each character has a brief, a few description variants (each makes 3 candidate voices on ElevenLabs Voice Design) and one audition everyone reads, with range: calm, threat or shout, quiet, a laugh. Sean picks on the casting page or asks for another round with notes; a picked candidate is saved to the account and recorded in cast_voices.json. Sean's note from the pilot (2026-10-27): many voices sounded 'very plain and modern'; every description asks for the 1880s frontier, textured and unpolished. Since 2026-10-27 each voice description is written from the man's model picture as well as his role (Sean: the stranger's first voices 'just didn't match his model').
common: Voice of a man on the 1880s American frontier, recorded close and dry like a film actor's dialogue, no music, no room echo. Unpolished and lived-in, not a modern announcer or narrator, not radio-smooth, no corporate or audiobook polish.

stranger.name: The stranger
stranger.brief: About forty (his model, bold_cowboy_s3: thick dark wavy hair, heavy dark moustache, a hard heavy-browed stare, clean white shirt and vest; a gentleman gunfighter or gambler). Sits at the card table and watches. Says little, never raises his voice, dry humour, unbothered by violence.

variants.text: A Southern gentleman gambler and gunman of about forty, Georgia-born. Rich, dark baritone, smooth on top with a rough edge underneath, soft-spoken and educated, every word controlled, quiet menace and dry wit.

A hard former lawman of about forty from Kansas. Firm, clear, deep baritone, plain frontier American speech with no strong drawl, flat and level, intense, a man who has killed and doesn't talk about it.

A strong Texas gunfighter in his early forties, handsome and sure of himself. Deep, warm baritone with grit in it and a light Texan drawl, unhurried, quietly confident, a hint of a smile in the voice, dangerous underneath.

stranger.audition: [calm] You're the one the sheriff sent. Sit down... you're making the room nervous. [low] Most folks come here to get lost. Some of 'em manage it. [dry chuckle] I've seen three men shot over this table, and every one of 'em thought he was quicker. Welcome to Salt Creek.

lyle.name: Hothead Lyle
lyle.brief: Thirties, outlaw. A quick temper held on a short leash; menace under every word; mean humour; explodes into shouting.

variants.text: A Texan outlaw in his thirties. Hard, raspy mid-range voice with a strong rural Texas twang. Coiled and dangerous, sneering, a nasty grin you can hear, snaps into loud shouting.
A Missouri bushwhacker turned gunman, about thirty-five. Rough, hoarse voice, thick backwoods accent, low and menacing when calm, ragged and loud when he shouts. Mean, mocking, unpredictable.
A big, heavy-set frontier outlaw in his late thirties. Low growling voice full of gravel, Southern drawl, slow menace, heavy breathing, a cruel laugh.

lyle.audition: [quiet, menacing] Deal 'em again. Your sleeve's wrong, Earl. Let's start there. [mocking] Square? You hear that, boys? He's been SQUARE. [shouting] He's behind the bar! Flush him out! [cold] You picked the wrong town, mister. [laughs] Come on out and I'll make it quick.

barkeep.name: Amos the barkeep
barkeep.brief: Forties. Tired, seen it all, keeps the peace by being dull and firm. Scared of Lyle and hiding it.

variants.text: A tired saloon keeper in his forties from Missouri. Plain, slightly nasal working-man's voice, flat Midwestern accent, weary and dry, firm when pushed, gets loud when he has to.
An Irish immigrant barkeep in his late forties, twenty years in the American West. Warm, gruff voice with a softened Irish lilt, world-weary, sardonic, can bellow across a room.
A heavy, balding frontier barman around fifty. Deep, gruff, phlegmy voice, rural American accent, slow and patient, long-suffering, a growl when he's angry.

barkeep.audition: [tired] Evening. What're you drinking? Ten cents a glass, a dollar a bottle, no credit, no exceptions. [shouting] Not in my saloon! Take it outside! [low, worried] If you're looking for the sheriff, try the doctor's. [sighs] He won't be up and about for a while.

cheater.name: Earl the card cheat
cheater.brief: Twenties. Charming, quick talker, all nerve until the gun comes out; then panic and begging.

variants.text: A young Kentucky cardsharp in his mid twenties. Light, bright, quick voice with a charming Southern drawl, cocky and smiling, talks fast, cracks into high panic when scared.
A Mississippi riverboat gambler of about twenty-five, slick and charming, smooth Southern accent with a showman's patter, easy laugh, voice breaks when he's frightened.
A skinny young drifter around twenty-two from rural Arkansas. Reedy, twangy voice, nervous energy, too much confidence, a cackling laugh, whiny and desperate when begging.

cheater.audition: [cheerful] Five card draw, nothing wild. You in, mister? [laughs] Lady luck's been sweet on me tonight, boys! [nervous laugh] Now hold on, hold on, I've been sat here square all night. [panicked] Lyle, wait, it was a joke! You can have it, have ALL of it! [begging] Please... I've got a sister in Abilene.
